## How the chart reads

A scatter chart with four reader-driven dimensions in one authored block: income on x, life expectancy on y, population on bubble size, and region on colour. Playback animates year as a categorical frame; a region button filters the visible bubbles. The chart's mark identity is preserved across frames: Europe always carries the same colour, Asia the same, Americas the same, so your eye follows a region through the century rather than reading a new chart each tick.

```chart
type: scatter
title: Income, life expectancy and population — a fictional snapshot across the century
subtitle: Values are invented for this authoring example; not an economic forecast.
data:
  csv: data/gapminder.csv
encoding:
  x: income
  y: life
  size: pop
  color: region
axes:
  x:
    label: GDP per capita (international dollars, invented)
    unit: $
  y:
    label: Life expectancy at birth
    unit: years
controls:
  - kind: playback
    id: year
    field: year
    label: Year
    speed: 900
    loop: true
    initial: "2000"
  - kind: filter
    id: region
    field: region
    label: Region
    options: [Europe, Asia, Americas, Africa]
    initial: Europe
    as: buttons
```

## How the controls behave

- The playback dimension holds the chart at the selected year, resolving to a row filter on the `year` column. Mark identity by region is preserved as the frame advances, so a reader can follow one region through the series without losing its colour.
- The region button group filters the visible rows one-of; it reads cleanly without a dashboard-wide picker.
- Reduced motion is a hard floor: when the reader's system prefers reduced motion the chart renders the end-of-playback frame and the scrubber stays usable, but auto-play does not start and inter-frame transitions are stepped rather than tweened.
